locator: cap.4 [69875]: esse earum non est absolutum, sed receptum et ideo limitatum et finitum ad capacitatem naturae recipientis
interpretation: In the second mode of essence (created intellectual substances) the esse of the thing is received and limited to the capacity of the receiving nature; c.3 [69874] likewise says the quiddity of an intelligence is in potency to the esse it receives. Read as: whatever principle a thing's esse is received in is that thing's own essence or nature. The passage names the receiving nature for the substances it discusses (and c.4 says composite substances have received esse too); extending 'the receiver is the thing's own nature' to every thing whose esse is received is the reading's generalization and is open. The reading concerns reception of esse, not of forms in matter, and does not assert that any esse is received.
